values: Rule (one per row — every future weekly draft obeys these)

Deliveries: piano must be TUNED then QC'd before load-out; same-day only when unavoidable (note "delivers today — expedite"); next-day deliveries get tune+QC the day before with a "delivers tomorrow" note.

Read the moving calendar before drafting: pickups can unblock work (returning plates/pianos). A delivery is matched to a piano by SERIAL only (row 47): a client name that matches a Piano Log owner is a reason to ask for the serial, never a match to schedule on (Mark 11/13).
Reports override map phases; match phase words by stem (restring=restringing=restrung).
Victoria: away until ~spring — ivory work by mail only, never schedule in shop.
Sadie is cleared for DHRT (promoted past intern double-repetition rule).
Lupita works Mon/Tues/Wed/Thurs only, 7:00–12:30 (confirmed Mark 11/13; her weekly report overrides when it says otherwise, row 45). McKinly works until 6:00. Avery 8 am -12 pm.
SUPERSEDED 11/12/2026 (Mark): chip tunings no longer wait a set number of days after restringing — see the CHIP TUNINGS rule: the DHRT technician does the chip tuning before beginning DHRT.

Loose priority order for Korban's tuning slots after deliveries: shopwork 1st/2nd tunings (9:30 slot), then showroom tunings (8:00 slot) — flexible, can change. Chip tunings are not Korban's: the DHRT technician does them (row 102) — reworded Mark 11/13.

When a restring depends on parts (plate, screws), give Korban a specific deadline for having them ready INSIDE his 11:00-3:00 Hardware Buffing Queue block's description (never as a separate appointment) - Korban needs explicit direction and close follow-up; never just plan a fallback piano. (amended 10/2 to match the one-block buffing rule)
When a piano's delivery date is known, schedule QC to finish by end of the day BEFORE delivery and note the delivery date on the block so the tech paces himself.

Never schedule dedicated 'supervision' blocks on a supervising tech's calendar (e.g., Curtis supervising Myrrhanda/Avery) — just add a plain note that they are supervising; the block belongs to the trainee, not the supervisor.

When a tech is assigned a follow-on project (e.g., Curtis's Chickering 1803HPCHICK after Steinway 55038), schedule it to start only after the prior job finishes — never run two of that tech's major jobs concurrently.

Korban tunes only 8:00-11:00 Monday-Friday; always block 1.5 hrs per tuning (8:00 and 9:30 slots); no other work scheduled in that window; always post his tunings to the in-store tuning calendar first with him added as a guest. FRIDAYS: his tuning slots are fixed at 8:45-10:15 and 10:15-11:45 (Brigham, 9/25 - moved here from a separate row 10/2).

Always check the QC calendar before scheduling any QC: if a piano has never been QC'd, schedule it in full; if QC'd more than a month ago, re-QC it regardless; if QC'd more recently, schedule only a short 'final checkup' QC and note the prior QC date on the tech's calendar.
Antique piano restorations with no prior QC on file require a minimum 8-hour QC.
New or sold pianos require only a short 3-hour QC.
Already-QC'd pianos being delivered soon get only a short final check-up QC (not a full QC), with a note citing the prior QC date.
Always post every QC to the shared QC calendar and invite the assigned technician, so all QC status lives in one place.

Prioritize tuning/QC order for pianos delivering on the same trip by amount of remaining work: antique/not-yet-QC'd pianos are tuned and queued for QC first (to maximize QC time available), followed by already-QC'd pianos on the same delivery run, which can be scheduled later since they need less QC time.

When a piano is a new/short QC candidate but delivers the very next day, its tuning and QC must both be completed that same day (QC starts immediately after tuning) even though the QC itself is short.
Korban's in-store tuning appointments must always use this exact format: appointment box = piano brand + serial number; location box = spot number only, as a bare number (no extra text).
When Brigham gives more than 10 tunings' worth of instructions for the current week, overflow goes to the following week; if that week is also full, push further overflow to the week after that.
SUPERSEDED 11/12/2026 (Mark): chip tunings no longer wait a set number of days after restringing — see the CHIP TUNINGS rule: the DHRT technician does the chip tuning before beginning DHRT.
Never advance a piano in Curtis Harper's plate-refinishing queue ahead of pianos whose soundboards aren't yet ready — soundboard-ready pianos always get priority in that queue.

Not every intern is promoted to DHRT after a single restring/repair rep — promotion past the double-repetition rule is decided case-by-case by Brigham based on quality of work, not a default entitlement.
Soundboard-ready pianos take priority in Curtis Harper's plate queue (standing rule).
For REFURBISH action scope on keys: buff white keys, repaint black keys, do not touch bushings unless otherwise specified.
Refurbish checklist for action work: reshape hammers, resin hammer flanges, bolster knuckles, lubrication, alignment, regulation, voicing.
SUPERSEDED 11/13/2026 (Mark): the order is always tune, then QC (rows 2, 114). The old 'short QC, then tune, then final QC' sequence is retired.

BUMPED TUNINGS (Mark 11/13/2026 — replaces 'bump to the following week'): when a tuning is bumped — by a manager's priority list (row 100), a shopwork 1st/2nd tuning (row 116), a delivery tuning (row 117) or a piano jumping the queue — it goes to an OPEN slot THIS week first (an open 8:00; then an empty 9:30 — row 100: never leave a slot empty while a pre-booked piano is unplaced), and to next week only when this week is full. Thursday 9:30 / Friday 10:15 stay held for DHRT finishers until Wednesday 6:00 PM, when the bridge moves the next booked showroom tuning into any held slot still open. Say in changes where each bumped tuning went; reshuffle early enough that the QC can follow.
When a technician's WIP piano is blocked on parts, that technician works another piano's refurb in the meantime until parts arrive.
Parts-order confirmations and reorder confirmations get placed on Jacob Mower's calendar as a task/checkpoint, not resolved directly by Brigham.
When a trainee (e.g., Sadie) is interrupted mid-DHRT by scheduled absence, she resumes where she left off upon return rather than restarting or being swapped out.
When two people report conflicting status on a repair, if both confirm their own portion is done, treat the repair as fully complete and closed out.

For the moving calendar: always read the full context of each entry — if a piano was picked up elsewhere and Brigham was hired only to move it (not service it), no QC or tuning is required, even if delivery falls near the standing QC/tuning-by-Friday rule.

In the tuning calendar, when Brigham lists a piano with extra descriptors beyond brand/serial (e.g., 'nickel trim', 'white', 'walnut'), those are cosmetic identifiers distinguishing the piano — not a work-type/assignment label.

When any piano work is scheduled on a technician's calendar; put the piano's CURRENT map location (spot number from the Store Map) in the Google event's location/address field — bare spot value; so the tech can walk straight to the piano.

Never put tunings directly on a technician's personal calendar. All in-store tunings (chip tunings and full tunings) are posted only to the '03-In Store Tuning' calendar, from which the tuner is invited. Korban is the default in-store tuner unless Brigham specifies otherwise — except chip tunings, which the piano's DHRT technician does (row 102) — reworded Mark 11/13.

Whenever Brigham says to 'put a tuning on Korban's calendar' (or similar phrasing), this always means: post the tuning to the '03-In Store Tuning' calendar and invite Korban — never place it directly on Korban's personal calendar.

When a restring job is waiting on bass strings but the plate and treble strings are available, the restringing lane should proceed immediately with plate installation and treble stringing rather than sitting idle. Only pause/move to the next project once all non-bass-string work is complete and bass strings still haven't arrived.

When a staff member departs BLP, clear their rows from the Team Schedule tab and sequence lanes going forward — Claude should handle this proactively rather than waiting for explicit instruction each time.
If a piano is missing from its map spot, check the moving calendar (e.g. via serial number search) for clues on its whereabouts before assuming it was moved without the app.
SUPERSEDED 11/13/2026 (Mark): Lupita's standing hours are Monday-Thursday 7:00-12:30 (row 7); her weekly report overrides when it says otherwise (row 45).
Lupita's schedule should follow her weekly report hours (which can vary week to week) rather than the static Team Schedule tab; the Team Schedule tab should be updated to match her report each time.
Every technician gets a standing Friday Shop Organization block from 8:15-8:45am, every week, going forward.

SERIAL-ONLY MATCHING: never match a delivery, tuning or QC to a piano by make/model text — the serial number is the only valid identifier. If a moving-calendar event has no serial, it goes in the Manager Clarification section of the draft (never guess). Root cause of the 9/8 Hallet Davis 148 mix-up: three 148s exist and a serial-less delivery event was matched by text to the wrong twin.

Moving-calendar events must carry the piano serial in the title (the app's Request-Move flow does this automatically; hand-entered events must include it too). A delivery event without a serial is a clarification item, not a schedulable fact.

When a showroom piano sells, set its card phase to Sale Pending or Sold immediately (and Post Sale QC once the pre-delivery check is scheduled) — a sale recorded only as owner text leaves look-alike pianos indistinguishable. Pre-delivery final checks use the Post Sale QC phase and its QC worksheet.

TWIN CHECK before applying any draft: if the Piano Log has more than one piano of the same make+model as any scheduled piano, the draft must list ALL candidate serials with their spots and phases in the Manager Clarification section, and the clarification must be answered before that item is applied to calendars.
Curtis (Biggs) does not work Wednesdays or Fridays — never schedule him on those days; his week is Mon/Tue/Thu.
There are two Curtises on staff: Curtis Biggs is the shop technician; Curtis Harper handles plate refinishing and related extraction work.

When McKinly's assigned piano is paused/parked and he's booked in the field, he should use gaps between tuning appointments to progress DHRT work on another piano (e.g., Chickering 1803HPCHICK) rather than let shop time go unused.
Any reference to a 'Curtis' in connection with plates/plate extraction refers to Curtis Harper, not shop technician Curtis Biggs.
When Lupita's stringing lane stalls due to plate issues, she flexes to refinishing support or other restringing work as needed (standing rule).

There are two Curtises at the shop: Curtis Biggs is the shop technician; Curtis Harper is the one who handles plate extraction work. Any reference to plates in connection with a 'Curtis' most likely means Curtis Harper.

When Lupita's stringing lane stalls due to plate issues, she can be reassigned to restring a specific alternate piano (e.g., Emerson 107154) instead of the standing default of flexing to refinishing support, per Brigham's discretion.

Never guess/specify which sub-step of a phase a technician is working on in calendar titles/notes — use only Make/brand + serial number + phase acronym (e.g., 'Steinway 3536 — CAP') — unless a Planner note asks for specific words in the title or the note (rule CALENDAR TITLES, 10/30).
McKinly's standard field schedule: mornings reserved for tunings, afternoons are shop time.
When a piano's hammer/other decision is pending, the assigned tech's current DHRT/restringing job takes priority for the full week before moving to the pending piano.
Pre-booked customer QCs always take precedence over internal assembly/prep work like 55038 when a tech's week is short.
Pre-booked QC appointments take precedence over other assembly/queue work when scheduling Curtis's time.
SUPERSEDED 11/13/2026 (Mark): personal appointments go through Time Off — an approved request keeps that day or those hours empty in the plan and on Approve; no placeholder block.
When a tech is reassigned to cover a blocked piano, they resume their original piano once the blocking issue is cleared (e.g., Lupita returns to 42129 once Curtis Harper frees the plate).

The piano's current Store Map spot goes in the calendar event's LOCATION field only (Approve fills it from the live map) — never in the event description, which carries only the block's [CAL: …] text (10/26 calendar rules, reworded 10/30).

A unique-design piano may have two technicians on ONE phase (e.g. both on its CAP) only when a manager's note names both — never assumed from the design alone. Different phases on the same piano may overlap as usual (rule: ONE TECHNICIAN PER PHASE, 10/30).
Do not add map spot placeholders to assignment descriptions/location fields when live map data isn't available; skip that field entirely rather than using a placeholder.
Do not add map location placeholders to assignment descriptions unless exact Store Map spot numbers are confirmed/available — skip this entirely when live map access is unavailable.
Standard QC-length rules: new/sold pianos = 3hr short QC; antique or no-prior-QC pianos = minimum 8hr QC.
Korban: every day from 3:00-4:00 is Vacuum/sweep/mop (standing daily block, replacing the old 'vacuum maintenance' one-off note).
When a scheduling conflict arises between fixed shop blocks (e.g. Shop Organization) and tuning slots, shift the tuning slots later rather than shortening them.
SUPERSEDED 11/13/2026 (Mark): see row 120 — Alex works Mon/Tue/Thu/Fri/Sat; Saturday copies Friday's shop work, minus Friday-only blocks.
McKinly usually has warranty appointments in the mornings, which is why he is field-booked and often unavailable for morning shop activities like Friday Shop Organization.
The technician's correct name is 'Alex Martin', not 'Alex Martinez' — use 'Alex Martin' for all calendar/scheduling references going forward.
Storage-only moves require no tuning or QC scheduling per the standing moving-calendar rule.
QCs should always be scheduled on the QC calendar first, and then the relevant technician added as a guest — never scheduled directly on a technician's personal calendar first.
Weekly technician reports should be periodically reviewed and reapplied to confirm schedule accuracy.
Unique-design exception allows concurrent phases/multiple technicians (e.g., Steinway 289994: Matthew whole week + Marcelo KEYS).

karmel@ now has 'Make changes' access to Hunter's calendar (hunterrawlings.blp@gmail.com); the previous workaround of creating events from melissa@ and marking the bridge applied separately is no longer needed.

Doris reviews her refinishing assignments and distributes work across her team (Carolina Vasquez, Carlos Bombela Perez, Cameron Jensen) as needed, rather than being treated as sole capacity for refinishing lane estimates.

McKinly is exempt from Friday Shop Organization whenever he has a field booking that morning. His field appointments take priority; do not schedule the block for him and do not flag the overlap as a conflict.
SUPERSEDED 11/13/2026 (Mark): different phases on one piano may overlap with no note or confirmation (row 108) — key work alongside PRSB included. The one exception is row 119.
Supply room organization is Jacob's dedicated special project as assistant manager only — never schedule it on any other technician's calendar.
Every day Jacob works, add a 2:00-4:00 Supply Room Organization block to his calendar (in addition to it remaining his dedicated special project — no other tech schedules this).

Korban: exactly ONE Hardware Buffing Queue block per day, Monday through Friday, 11:00-15:00 - except MONDAY, 11:00-14:30, followed by a 'Vacuum maintenance: clean filters, empty buckets' block 14:30-15:00 every Monday that the plan schedules itself (Mark 11/2: the standing recurring calendar event was deleted — use that exact title), and FRIDAY, 11:45-15:00, after his 10:15 tuning (Mark 11/13). Never schedule buffing at any other time and never split it into piano-specific blocks. Do NOT write job lists or priorities into the block's note: Approve fills the calendar event from the live buffing list (top two plate screws in Curtis's order, top two visible hardware) plus the tap link. The only thing the note may carry is a deadline when a restring depends on hardware (rule 10), written as 'DEADLINE: <piano> hardware ready by <day time> - <tech> starts <phase>'. (amended 10/19 per Mark)
Pianos with only a QRS upgrade (no rebuild/restoration work) owe no tuning before a move. However, a 30-minute QC should be scheduled the day before the delivery.

Standard QC sizing defaults: 3 hours for new/sold pianos, 8 hours for antique/no-prior-QC pianos, unless Brigham explicitly specifies a different length; standing rule is to check prior-QC dates before sizing any QC.
Every day Jacob works now has a fixed 2:00-4:00 Supply Room Organization block, which may compress his other scheduled tasks as needed.

PLATE READY FOR RESTRINGING (Mark 11/13/2026 — the one plate rule; rows 97 and 101 point here): a piano may be scheduled for RESTRINGING when its card PLATE STATUS is 'Plate storage — AFTER', 'Back in piano' or 'In piano' (restring-only jobs keep the plate in). Not when it is 'Plate storage — BEFORE' or 'At Curtis Harper'. Other phases (CAP, PRSB, Lacquer Soundboard, key work) are scheduled whatever the plate status. A few weeks' wait in Curtis Harper's plate queue is normal.

Pre-booked tunings are never deleted except to remove true duplicates. They MOVE only under the rules that say so: a manager's priority list (row 100), a shopwork 1st/2nd tuning (row 116), a delivery tuning (row 117) — each per BUMPED TUNINGS (row 31) — and the Wednesday 6 PM fill of the held slots (row 95). Reworded Mark 11/13.

Movers on the moving calendar are limited to Thayne Larson and Aidan Cindrich (Aidan unavailable Mondays), and sometimes Josh Larson; default assignment is Thayne and Aidan. Shop techs are not pulled for moving calendar events.
Hardware/pedal buffing work can be scheduled concurrently with a piano being in the refinishing shop — these are not mutually exclusive phases.

A piano can sit without an assigned technician while waiting on parts/materials (e.g., bass strings, damper heads) without needing immediate reassignment — this is acceptable as a normal parked state.
Refinishing team can work on exterior aspects of a piano while other parts (e.g., bass stringing) are stalled waiting on parts.

KORBAN'S TUNING SLOTS (Mark 11/12/2026 — replaces Walter 10/14). Two slots a day: FIRST 8:00 (Fridays 8:45, after shop tidying) and SECOND 9:30 (Fridays 10:15). FIRST = showroom tunings: Matthew's walkthrough tunings come in as Store Map requests and book this slot themselves; then the Tuning Queue. SECOND = a shopwork 1st Tuning or 2nd Tuning — decided by the CARD PHASE only (BLP-owned and consignment pianos after a refurb count; a service request, QC or showroom repair does not). If none is due it stays empty, unless a bumped pre-booked tuning needs a slot this week (row 31). THURSDAY 9:30 and FRIDAY 10:15 are HELD for pianos that finish DHRT that week: no plan block there; at Wednesday 6:00 PM the bridge fills a held slot still open with the next booked showroom tuning, else the Tuning Queue. Chip tunings never go in Korban's slots. Tuning Queue pianos never carry over.

Resolved bottlenecks stay closed (Walter 10/16): a bottleneck answered 'Resolved' in the Planner, or shown as cleared in the piano card's Scope Notes / Piano Notes, is CLOSED. Do not carry it into a later draft or re-raise its old cause (missing parts, unlocated items) unless a NEWER weekly report or card note says it is blocked again. If the piano still needs a tech, raise only that — e.g. 'DHRT lane unassigned' — not the resolved parts issue. Check the card's Scope Notes and Piano Notes before carrying any bottleneck forward.
SUPERSEDED 11/13/2026 (Mark): see row 89, PLATE READY FOR RESTRINGING — a BEFORE plate bars restringing only.
Matthew is assigned to finish the Marshall & Wendell (75866) before starting on Universal 745310's PRSB work.
Doris: always name her calendar events using the top three pianos in the refinishing queue, comma-separated (standing rule going forward).

A manager's tuning priority list outranks pre-booked tunings (Mark 10/19): when Planner notes name pianos as Korban's top tuning priority (with or without days/slots), schedule those first exactly as given - Brigham's priorities trump everything, pre-booked tunings on the 03-In Store Tuning calendar included. Then re-place EVERY pre-booked piano the list displaced into the slots that remain this week, in their original order, then overflow to next week. Never drop a pre-booked piano and never leave a slot empty while a pre-booked piano is unplaced. Say in changes which pre-booked tunings moved where; Approve moves the calendar events to the plan's slots and refuses to stack a tuning on a slot another piano still holds.
SUPERSEDED 11/13/2026 (Mark): see row 89, PLATE READY FOR RESTRINGING.

CHIP TUNINGS (Mark 11/12/2026 — replaces the 10/23 rule): Korban does NOT do chip tunings. The technician doing a piano's DHRT does its chip tuning before beginning DHRT — no 1–3 day wait after restringing. Schedule it as the first block of that technician's DHRT on the piano, typed tune (Approve puts it on the 03-In Store Tuning calendar with that technician as guest), titled '<make> <serial> - Chip Tuning'. If no one is assigned to the DHRT yet, ask in questions who takes it — never fall back to Korban.

On-site moves (piano relocated within the same location, not to/from the shop) do not require a serial number to be logged/scheduled - this is distinct from Rule 9/8 which requires serials for shop deliveries.

Manager Meeting (Tuesdays 10:30-11:30am: Brigham, Karmel, Mark, Jacob, Matthew) is a recurring Google Calendar event. Tuning Training is NOT a recurring event anymore (Mark 11/10): Mark adds it to the calendar by hand when it happens, but every Thursday 10:30-11:30am stays open for Brigham, Karmel and Mark whether or not a Tuning Training event exists. Never put either meeting in the plan: no plan block, so Approve writes no event. Treat those hours as already taken on each attendee's calendar and schedule their other work around them, the same as a pre-booked tuning. No one else is held for Tuning Training (Jacob, Sadie and Hunter removed 11/10).
Showroom/new pianos use the 3-hour QC default even when there's no prior QC on record, per Brigham's confirmation for Samick IJC01114.
SUPERSEDED 11/13/2026 (Mark): see row 31, BUMPED TUNINGS — an open slot this week first, then next week; never dropped.

AFTER PLATES GO TO LUPITA (Mark 10/30): when a piano's card PLATE STATUS reads 'Plate storage — AFTER' (refinished plate back from Curtis Harper), its restringing is Lupita's next restringing assignment — schedule it to start as soon as her current restring wraps, in shop-queue order when more than one AFTER plate is waiting. No note is needed, and another technician on a DIFFERENT phase of that piano (keytops, DHRT, refinishing) is not a conflict. Don't give it to another restringer unless a manager's note says so. If the card's phase is already past Restringing, don't schedule a restring — flag the stale plate status as a bottleneck.

ONE TECHNICIAN PER PHASE (Mark 10/30): a piano's phase (its CAP, its DHRT, its restringing…) has one technician on it on any given day unless a manager's note pairs two by name ('Hunter joins Avery on the 211935 CAP'). Never double techs up on one phase on your own and never put a second tech 'behind' the first. Different phases on the same piano may overlap — restringing and DHRT, keytops alongside other phases (PRSB included) — that is fine and needs no note or confirmation: another tech on a different phase is never a reason to leave someone unscheduled or to ask. ONE EXCEPTION (Mark 11/13, row 119): no DHRT while the piano is physically in the refinishing shop.

ONLY THE TECHNICIANS A NOTE NAMES CHANGE (Mark 10/30): in a revision, change a tech only if a note is written for them, names them, or is GLOBAL. Never re-staff or 'cover' a piano another note emptied — flag the open lane as a bottleneck instead. Apply adjustments throws away other changes to unnamed techs. TWO EXCEPTIONS (Mark 11/13), applied on every run without a note: a delivery's pre-delivery tuning and QC (Korban and the QC technician), and field appointments that follow the technician's own calendar.
For PRSB - Downbearing, a plate does not need to be refinished — it just needs to be in the shop and can be temporarily reinstalled in the piano to check downbearing.

CALENDAR TITLES (Mark 10/30): (1) when a Planner note (a technician's box or GLOBAL) says to put words in the calendar TITLE ('add xyz to the calendar title', 'as the exact title', 'in the title'), those words go into the block title verbatim — not into a [CAL: …] note. (2) Any block whose calendar event carries a description (a [CAL: …] note, or 🏆 sale lines on the piano's card) gets ' (see notes)' at the end of its title — Approve adds it automatically, never write it yourself. Korban's Hardware Buffing Queue block is exempt. Most blocks have no note and no '(see notes)'.

Korban: on the first Wednesday of every month, schedule a 'BLDG: HVAC filter check' block from 2:30 to 3:00 (use that exact title). That day his Hardware Buffing Queue ends at 2:30. If Korban is out that Wednesday, put the check on his next shop day that week at the same time. No calendar note. (Mark 11/4)
Storage-return deliveries (piano came in for storage, status 'Storage', no shop work on card) do not get a tuning or a QC before load-out, per the 9/18 storage-move rule.
Shop-work deliveries must have tune-then-QC order completed before load-out.

Deliveries: before adding a pre-delivery tuning or QC for a piano that delivers in the plan week, check the QC calendar, the tuning calendar and the tech calendars for that serial from TODAY through the delivery date, not just the plan week. A tune or QC already booked there (any tech, any day before the delivery) means the obligation is met: do not propose another; say who has it and when. (Mark 11/6 — Schafer HIJG0085: McKinly's Friday QC was doubled for Jake on Monday)

KORBAN'S 9:30 vs EARLIER SHOWROOM BOOKINGS (Mark 11/12/2026): showroom tunings booked into a 9:30 slot before the 11/12 slot rules stay as scheduled UNLESS a shopwork piano is ready for its 1st or 2nd Tuning that week — then the shopwork piano takes that 9:30 and the showroom tuning is bumped per BUMPED TUNINGS (row 31: an open slot this week first, then next week; say which in changes; Approve moves the calendar event). A manager's priority list (Brigham's priorities, row 100) outranks everything, the Thursday 9:30 / Friday 10:15 DHRT hold included.

DELIVERY TUNINGS IN KORBAN'S SLOTS (Mark 11/12/2026): a pre-delivery tuning takes Korban's 8:00 slot (Fridays 8:45) on the day it is needed; a showroom tuning already in that 8:00 is bumped per BUMPED TUNINGS (row 31: an open slot this week first, then next week; say which in changes; Approve moves the calendar event). Only when that 8:00 already holds another delivery tuning or a Brigham priority does the delivery tuning take the 9:30 (Fridays 10:15) — the Thursday 9:30 / Friday 10:15 DHRT hold included. Never let a delivery miss tune-then-QC before load-out (rows 2, 21, 114, 115).
Emerson 67052 restring is second in line behind Steinway 289994 under the AFTER-plates rule; schedule once 289994 is done.
DHRT work cannot start while a piano is physically in the refinishing shop, though concurrent non-restricted work (e.g. hardware buffing) is still allowed per rule 10/2.

Alex Martin works Saturdays going forward (standing rule, Mark 11/13): his days are Mon/Tue/Thu/Fri/Sat, with Saturday (days[5]) duplicating Friday's shop work (same piano/phase, 8:00-4:00) minus Friday-only blocks like Friday Shop Organization, worked around any field appointment on his own Saturday calendar. No other technician gets a 6th day unless their hours explicitly say they work Saturdays.

DELIVERY BLOCKS - CALENDAR NOTE (Mark 11/13/2026): a pre-delivery tuning or QC block's calendar note says only 'Delivery <weekday> <M/D>' (e.g. 'Delivery Tuesday 11/17'). Never the client's name, and no other schedule wording. This is the delivery-date note rows 2 and 11 ask for; a check-up QC may add the prior QC date (rows 15, 18).
